Subject: PayBridge SDK & credentialing — post-demo roadmap and POC asks

Alex — great demo today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned: 

Summary of what we covered
- Use-case: server-side enrichment + searchable embeddings + a small reranker for customer support routing; structured output to populate downstream ticket fields and call an internal tool for account lookups.
- Traffic profile: expect bursts (50–100 QPS) with median seq len ~128 tokens, peak up to 512 for some transcripts.
- Security posture: PayBridge prefers server-to-server auth; security team asked about rotation and audit trails.

Open questions for PayBridge
1) Preferred auth pattern for production POC: API keys vs OAuth2/JWT service account vs ephemeral tokens?
2) Do you need SAML/OIDC SSO for the console or just programmatic service credentials?
3) Can you provide a small sample dataset (anonymized) for embedding quality checks (5–10 example texts)?

Attachments I’m including: 1) redwood-auth-patterns.pdf — short comparison of our recommended flows, 2) paybridge-integration-requirements.xlsx — simple template for workload and SLOs.

Suggested next steps (with owners)
- PayBridge: share which auth pattern you prefer & the security questionnaire (Alex) — target: Wed 3/21
- Redwood: tech kickoff to walk the SDK, sample repo, and key rotation runbook (Dylan + Ben) — propose 60m slot next week
- Redwood: run a quick embedding/reranker smoke test once we have sample data (Marissa)

If you can confirm auth preference and a 60-minute slot for the technical kickoff, we’ll lock dates.

Cheers,

Thanks, Marissa — good summary. A few quick replies: 

1) Auth preference: our security team leans toward JWT service accounts (server-to-server) with short-lived tokens (<=1h) and automated rotation. We prefer not to embed long-lived API keys in our backend.
2) Console access: will need SSO via our Okta SAML for any human admin users. Programmatic access only for the initial POC.
3) Sample data: I’ll drop anonymized transcripts + a short csv of customer categories by EOD Monday.

I’ve attached our SOC2 questionnaire — security@paybridge.com will follow up with more details if you need evidence for any controls.

Timeline: can we start a two-week POC (integration + embedding quality eval) the week of 3/27? If so, we’ll aim to have the sample data and the security questionnaire in the next 48 hours.

—Alex

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: PayBridge SDK & credentialing — post-demo roadmap and POC asks

Alex — perfect, thanks for the quick turnaround and the questionnaire. A few technical notes to make the POC smooth based on your preference for JWT service accounts: 

Recommended production pattern (short summary)
- For server-to-server calls from PayBridge backend -> Redwood: use OAuth 2.0 JWT Bearer (RFC 7523) with signed assertions from a PayBridge service account. Redwood accepts JWT assertion exchange and issues short-lived ephemeral tokens scoped to the requested model/route.
- Rotation: we recommend rotating the service account keys every 30 days for production; for the POC a 90-day cadence is fine. Redwood can support automated key rollover via a signed-keys endpoint and will log key_id usage for audit.
- Backup flow: we can enable an ephemeral API-key exchange (short-lived token issued by Redwood after a one-time mutual TLS handshake) if you need an alternate rollback path during the POC.

SDK/dev ergonomics
- Our SDK has a sample helper for JWT assertion creation and automatic token refresh; we’ll share a minimal sample repo during the kickoff. You can also use our REST token-exchange endpoint if you prefer to avoid the SDK.
- Embeddings/reranker note: to reduce costs and latency we’ll recommend accepting 16-bit quantized model variants for the reranker in the POC and evaluating accuracy on your sample set. Expect a simple embedding eval to take 2–3 hours for a 200-example set.

Security/audit
- Redwood retains audit logs for token exchanges and per-request model routes; we can push log snapshots to your S3 or stream to your SIEM depending on your controls.

Proposed schedule
- 3/20–3/22: tech kickoff (60m) — proposed attendees: Dylan (infra lead), Ben (solutions eng), Alex + security rep
- 3/27–4/7: two-week POC (integration + embedding/reranker eval)

Action items before kickoff
- PayBridge: share sample data + confirm Okta SAML admin users (Alex)
- Redwood: prepare SDK sample repo + token-exchange runbook (Dylan, Ben)

I’ll send a calendar invite for 3/21 and adjust if the time doesn’t work.

Best,
Marissa

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: prep for PayBridge POC — SDK sample & key-ops runbook

Ben/Dylan — quick internal note after Alex’s answers. Key asks for the kickoff and POC prep: 

1) SDK sample repo (owner: Ben) — prepare a minimal node + python example that does:
  - JWT assertion creation (from PayBridge-provided private key)
  - token-exchange call to Redwood and refresh loop
  - a single generate call with structured output turned on and an embeddings example call
  - README that documents env vars we’ll ask PayBridge to set (OKTA_METADATA_URL, SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY_PATH -> we'll ask for the public-key thumbprint for verification).

2) Key rotation/runbook (owner: Dylan) — 1 page runbook covers:
  - recommended rotation cadence (POC: 90d; Prod: 30d)
  - rolling rekey strategy with no downtime (dual-key acceptance window for 10 min)
  - automated alert criteria (failed JWT signature X times, repeated token-exchange rate limits)
  - fallback: enable ephemeral API-key exchange for POC rollback and how to flip traffic back via routing policy.

3) Audit & logs (owner: Monica) — short checklist for pushing token exchange logs to PayBridge S3 and what fields they need (key_id, kid, token_issue_ts, caller_ip, model_route).

Timing: can you each have first drafts by EOD Monday (3/19)? I’ll own coordination and the kickoff invite. If anything there seems off or you need an alternate owner, flag me.

Thanks — Marissa
